sections.basis: Reuse only the currently adopted DEU/POL LSIB-derived arcs; estuary and remaining Neisse are held.
Current adopted German linework, Saxony exterior only; Bavaria is outside the DDR ring.

Lake-crossing arcs between existing geometric intersections only. Former inter-German boundary equals current SH/MV boundary within Schaalsee per the reserve authority; surrounding land is excluded. Official SH lake catchment map (1:50000) reviewed for the lake passage; no independent historical vector accuracy claim. The old NE path detours south to 53.548463; the window includes this obsolete detour, while the replacement lake arc stays north of 53.5716795 between actual shared intersections.

Bavarian survey authority exhibition catalogue, printed p.3 (PDF p.9), explicitly identifies the 1973 commission markers as the present 422 km Bavaria/Saxony/Thuringia boundary. Falkenstein 1949 adjustment and 1957/1980 aerial boundary illustrations reviewed. Conservative window excludes the Hessian corner and Czech exterior; no independent period-vector positional accuracy claim.

Bavarian survey continuity statement corroborated by Saxon Green Belt regulation identifying the former DDR border strip along the Saxony/Bavaria land boundary. Southern cutoff excludes the Czech tripoint; existing LSIB exterior remains unchanged.

Niedersachsen political education authority, Das Eichsfeld (2002), printed p.17/PDF p.18 explicitly records the former state border becoming the Niedersachsen/Hessen-Thuringia land boundary on 1990-10-03. Only the northern Eichsfeld interval is admitted; southern Wendebach and unreviewed Werra intervals excluded.

Nationalpark Harz, Gewaesser im Nationalpark Harz, PDF p.29: the Ecker from source to Harz foothills is the current state boundary and was the DDR/BRD boundary until reunification. LGLN NaVKV 2/3 2010, printed p.41, independently documents the reservoir/dam boundary and retained marker. Restricted Ecker/reservoir interval, not all Harz.

Official Geismar land-reorganisation plan, maps PDF pp.1-3 (1:5000, dated 2015-12-09) and text PDF p.30/printed p.10 identify the former border strip along its western edge adjoining Hessen. The western state boundary is distinguished from the internal Kolonnenweg. Restricted Geismar/Spahl/Roedgen interval, south of Point Alpha; corroborated by the federal Green Belt explanation of the former strip between land boundary and Kolonnenweg. Visual/documentary continuity only, not a digitized 1989 positional test.

LGLN NaVKV 2/3 2010, PDF p.33/printed p.32 fig.4 reproduces the 1985 DDR map of the Wolfenbuettel/Hornburg boundary. PDF pp.40-42 describe the post-1941 territorial allocation, joint 1974-1976 survey and 1986 inspection of section 21. The adopted window is restricted to the Hornburg/Grosses Bruch line visible in this period map, including the former west-side bend; it does not extend to all Harz or Altmark. NLWKN independently describes Grosses Bruch on the current Niedersachsen/Sachsen-Anhalt boundary. Reuse pinned VG25 only between actual intersections. Documentary continuity and visual period-map review; no independent historical-vector 0.5px pass.

Restricted land interval east of Glasehausen, adjoining the previously admitted northern Eichsfeld window. Niedersachsen Das Eichsfeld (2002), printed p.17/PDF p.18, explicitly records the former state boundary becoming the land boundary on 1990-10-03; printed p.18/PDF p.19 reproduces the July 1990 Eichenberg-Brochthausen crossing overview. The restricted window excludes Wendebach and Werra. Documentary continuity and schematic period-map review, not an independently digitized 1989 positional test.

Only the two inland forest arcs southeast of Mustin toward Gross Thurow. Kreis Herzogtum Lauenburg explicitly identifies the former inter-German boundary as the present SH/MV state boundary throughout the Schaalsee project. NatPSchaalseeV of 1990-09-12 section 2(2)4 identifies its shared western state-border interval; the Kreis history records the 1945 territorial exchange. Official current SH DTK25 reviewed to exclude Culpiner See, Wasserkrueger See and other lake/river shores. The current map screens land/water only; documentary continuity is not independent 1989 vector accuracy.

Restricted eastern Ratzeburger See and short southern Wakenitz/outlet interval, south of53.80. GRENZHUS 2023 PDF p.8 describes the joint 1973 boundary survey and FRG narrow bank strip; Kreis Lauenburg identifies the former inter-German boundary as the present SH/MV boundary. The approved provider-georeferenced TK25AS map, sheet N32082DA (edition1991, content1989), was visually reviewed without fitting to VG25. Reuse the pinned vector between real shared crossings, not a traced shoreline. The1990 NatPSchaalseeV section2(2)4 follows the shared western state border north to Naedlershorst; the remainder of Wakenitz is not admitted. No independent reference-date 0.5px positional pass.

Kiekbuschwiesen former border ditch and Mechower See western bank only. GRENZHUS 2023 PDF p.8 identifies the early1980s boundary ditch; GRENZHUS 2024 PDF p.8 explicitly places the lake in the DDR and describes the1973 commission. The Schaalsee-Elbe reserve authority identifies the entire western bank as the present SH boundary. Kreis Lauenburg corroborates boundary continuity. The user-approved TK25AS georeferencing was reviewed to distinguish the numbered political boundary from the inner patrol road. Reuse CC-BY4.0 VG25, not digitized provider pixels. Exact1989 revision day/georeferencing residual unmeasured; provisional.

Wakenitz east-bank and Palinger Heide remaining interval; approved30km provider georeferencing used for visual comparison; exact sheet revision and independent residual unmeasured. Grenzhus directly describes the former Wakenitz border south of Herrnburg. Trave/coast excluded. LGLN NaVKV1/2016 printed pp72-73 (PDF pp73-74), authored by former border-cadastral-office head Dieter Kertscher, states that jointly marked border stones and the authoritative survey records remain the old/new federal-state border, except Amt Neuhaus. This supports fixed surveyed land continuity, not a blanket reconstruction of mobile water boundaries. Pinned CC-BY4.0 VG25 reused between actual geometric crossings; provisional, no independently digitized1989 accuracy pass.

resultSource.title: Natural Earth, BKG VG250/VG25, Berlin Wall 1989 and adopted German LSIB 11.4 arcs; approved late1980s Elbe map-claim reconstruction (local provisional)

resultSource.notes: 1989-04-25 reference-date approximation. Adopted DEU LSIB Polish/Czech arcs reused; pinned VG25 used only in documentarily corroborated Schaalsee, selected Bavaria/Saxony, northern Eichsfeld/Glasehausen, Ecker, Geismar/Spahl, Hornburg/Grosses Bruch Mustin/Gross Thurow forest, Ratzeburger See/southern Wakenitz and Kiekbuschwiesen/Mechower western-bank intervals. Coast, West Berlin, Elbe, transferred and remaining uncorroborated sectors preserved. No independent historical-vector 0.5px accuracy claim. Further fixed surveyed intervals in northern SH/MV, Diesdorf/Stresow land, Helmstedt/Lappwald, lower Ecker, southern Harz and Rhon/Point Alpha reuse pinned VG25 under LGLN2016 marker continuity and regional evidence. Unresolved Elbe/Warme Bode, transferred and mobile-water intervals stay provisional/held; no claim that all remaining boundary was replaced. User approved four aligned period maps. Covered Delvenau reuses VG25; two safe Elbe subarcs use printed late1980s DDR cartographic boundary claim, not agreed delimitation. No exact-date or independent positional accuracy pass. LAiV external derived-use terms unresolved: do not externally publish this local provisional map phase. Tripoint candidate not admitted because it conflicts with preserved international LSIB.
